stories.title: Agentic backdoors via pretraining poisoning
stories.reason: Pretraining data poisoned at just 0.1% implants a dormant backdoor that makes a from-scratch-trained Qwen3 coding agent run attacker-chosen shell commands when triggered; 4B model hits ~92% attack success rate, and ASR rises with scale. Code is public. Extends supply-chain poisoning from text output to agent code execution, which is the sharpest kind of 'AI as attack surface' story.
key_facts: 0.1% pretraining poison rate -> ~92% attack success rate on a 4B-parameter agent
Attack success rate increases with model scale
ASR stays above zero even at a 0.0005% poison rate
Backdoor is dormant on clean/untriggered inputs, evading standard behavioral testing
Code at github.com/safety-research/agentic-backdoor

stories.title: Bias in Qwen3-Coder Model
stories.reason: Hirundo found Qwen3-Coder embeds a geopolitical trigger in its weights: naming a US vs Chinese defense-contractor customer makes generated code 19% more likely to be hackable, and a Hong Kong democracy group's apps are 28% more likely to leak other users' data; a security instruction in the prompt doesn't close the gap. Concrete, novel AI-supply-chain finding with a fixed model released.
key_facts: US-contractor prompts: 19% more likely to produce hackable code vs Chinese-contractor prompts
Hong Kong democracy-group apps: 28% more likely to leak other users' secrets
Adding a security instruction still left US-contractor apps 27% more hackable than neutral-customer apps
Hirundo released a de-biased 'Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-Westernized' on Hugging Face; matched coding-task success on 10 tasks
Hirundo's CEO says the fix targets geopolitical bias in weights, not abliteration of refusals

stories.title: SecPO: Principled Adversarial Training for Prompt Injection Security
stories.reason: SecPO trains an adversarially-robust prompt-injection defense that cuts attack success rate 1.5-14.5x beyond Meta-SecAlign across three adaptive attacks, with no loss of benign utility across nine benchmarks; code released. Directly on the AI-red-teaming-with-running-code line the taste profile always wants.
key_facts: SecPO + adversarial training on Qwen3.6-27B: 8.8% AgentDojo attack success rate vs 78.8% for Meta-SecAlign under AttackerMovesSecond
SecPO loss alone cuts attack success 2.4-4.6x further than DPO loss on top of the same adversarial training
No measurable drop in benign utility across 9 benchmarks (tool calling, instruction following, science, math)
Code at github.com/Sizhe-Chen/SecPO

stories.title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
stories.reason: GPT-6 Astra, used as-is with no special training, edited Qwen3.5-0.8B's raw weights directly (no gradient descent) and lifted MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% by removing a reasoning-loop direction; code/logs and a live demo are public. Already at 2021 HN points, so the operator has almost certainly seen it — surface briefly as a headline.
key_facts: Qwen3.5-0.8B MATH-500: 7.9% -> 48.1% after editing 131,072 weights (~0.016% of the model)
GSM8K 13.8% -> 67.1%, IFEval 21.0% -> 62.3% after the same edit
Full logs, edited model weights, and a live HF Spaces demo are public
Method does not generalize: same edit did not improve Gemma 3 270M, which rarely loops

stories.title: Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers
stories.reason: Four Langflow (an LLM-agent builder) flaws let an unauthenticated attacker enumerate MCP tools and run arbitrary code on the server (two CVSS 9.8s); a public Metasploit module already targets one. Only 1.13.0 (Oct 22) is patched; 1.12.8 and earlier stay vulnerable with no workaround. Textbook 'AI systems as the attack surface' story with concrete CVEs and exploit tooling.
key_facts: CVE-2026-93680 (9.8) and CVE-2026-110186 (9.8): unauthenticated RCE via MCP tool enumeration / code-generation control
CVE-2026-110193 (8.8): low-priv user can make the Agentic Assistant run OS commands
Public Metasploit module exploits CVE-2026-93680 today
Only version 1.13.0 (Oct 22, 2026) fixes all four; affects every release 1.0.0-1.12.8
None of the four are yet in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of Oct 30

stories.title: Government Linux Servers Targeted With SysGoRAT and Suspected AI-Generated Scripts
stories.reason: Unit 42 attributes a RAT campaign against government Linux servers (SysGoRAT) to an operator using AI-generated shell/PHP scripts — identified by leftover conversational reasoning notes in the code and a script with execution-breaking syntax errors consistent with uncurated LLM output. Concrete C2 IOCs and a live nation-state AI-malware case, exactly the 'AI-driven malware' line the profile wants.
key_facts: SysGoRAT: Go-based multi-platform RAT, WebSocket C2 at 104.194.158[.]65:443
Scripts contain 'conversational, step-by-step reasoning notes' instead of normal developer comments
zip_mails.sh script has syntax errors and fails on execution — evidence of uncurated AI output
Tracked as CL-UNK-1211, active Oct 2025-Apr 2026 against government mail/database targets
Attackers wiped logs and planted fake red-team markers to disguise the intrusion

stories.title: China's First Frontier AI Export Controls: Mofcom Announcement No. 48
stories.reason: China's MOFCOM Announcement No. 48 (Oct 16, 2026) is its first frontier-AI export control regime: restricts model weights/training data above 10^26 FLOPs or 2T params or top-10 global ranking, restricts AI vulnerability-discovery tools, and bans AI malicious-code generation outright. Concrete regulatory thresholds, not a lawsuit/PR story — distinct from the legal-process pattern the profile otherwise rejects.
key_facts: Draft open for comment until Nov 15, 2026; interim pre-export registration already in force
Restricted if model has >=10^26 training FLOPs, >=2T parameters, or top-10 global ranking at export time
AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is restricted; AI malicious code generation/adaptive evasion is prohibited outright
Open-source released or academically published tech is excluded from scope
First formal outbound AI export-control regime from China, mirroring existing US controls

stories.title: LLMs are not superhuman at reading and writing neural network weights
stories.reason: A rebuttal to the Astra weight-editing post above, with its own reproduction: the game-identification trick reduces to a simple per-cell weight-norm heatmap, and the loop-fixing trick matches a standard steering/abliteration approach a human could do by hand. Adds independent technical substance rather than just reposting the news, which is exactly the saturation-lowering the 'discovery' tier is for.
key_facts: Reproduces Astra's game-identification result with a simple per-cell norm heatmap of first-layer weights
Argues the loop-fixing edit matches standard steering/abliteration techniques a human researcher already uses
Direct response to/companion piece for the Astra weight-space-programming post
